div.head: Grið 3
div.ab: ⁊ hwilum wæran heafodstedas ⁊ healice hadas micelre mæðe ⁊ munde wyrðe ⁊ griðian mihton þa, þe þæs beðorf[ton] ⁊ þærto sohtan, áá be ðære mæðe, þe þærto gebyrede.
And hwilum wæran heafodstedas and healice hadas micelre mæðe and munde wyrðe and griðian mihton þa þe þæs beðorfton and þærto sohtan, aa be ðære mæðe þe þærto gebyrede.

Und einstmals waren Hauptstätten und hohe Stände zu grosser Würde und Schutzgewalt berechtigt und konnten diejenigen mit Sonderfrieden schützen, die dessen bedurften und dorthin [sich wendend Schutz] suchten, immer gemäss dem Range, der dort[igem Schutz] zukam.

And formerly chief places and high ranks were entitled to great dignity and protective authority, and could protect with special peace those who needed it and sought [protection, turning] there, always according to the rank that belonged to [the protection of] that place.

And it once was that capital cities and those of high rank were entitled to great privileges and could offer protection and sanctuary to those who needed it and sought it there, always in keeping with the privileges that belonged thereto.
div.note: The final syllable of ‘beðorf[ton]’ is hidden by the binding. Liebermann compares Geþyncðo 1.; T: corrected against Rabin, DOML 66 (2020), p. 22 (before: ‘And hwilum wæran heafodstedas and healice hadas micelre mæðe and munde wyrðe and griðian mihton þa þe pæs beðorfton and þærto sohtan, aa be þære mæðe þe þærto gebyrede.’); AY: corrected against Rabin p. 22 / 23, October 2026 (was “∅”, now “Manuscripts: G = London, British Library, Cotton MS Nero A.i, fol. 92v–95v. |”); AZ: added from Rabin p. 22 / 23, October 2026 (Rabin’s note to the translation)
Manuscripts: G = London, British Library, Cotton MS Nero A.i, fol. 92v–95v.
beðorfton: final three letters concealed by binding. This reading follows Liebermann.

3–5: The nostalgic tone of clauses 3 through 5 recalls the similar evocation of an idealized past in the opening clauses of the first item in The Compilation on Status, On the Ranks of People and Law, a text likely composed at approximately the same time as this one. It also highlights the present-day deterioration in ecclesiastical status, which made necessary the injunctions that follow.

note.seg: ton durch Binden unsichtbar; beþurfon Thorpe [falsch laut folg. sohtan]
ton hidden by the binding; beþurfon Thorpe [wrong, as the following sohtan shows]

Verf. will nicht etwa das Recht als jetzt abgeschafft hinstellen, sondern nur als ehrwürdig alt (vgl. Gl altes Recht), durch Zitat belegbar und früher besser beobachtet, jetzt praktisch ungenügend befolgt; vgl. o. S. 257 n. 10

The author is not trying, say, to present the law as now abolished, but only as venerably old (cf. Gl altes Recht), attestable by quotation and better observed in the past, but now insufficiently obeyed in practice; cf. above p. 257 n. 10

heafodstede setzt Ælfred für capitolium des Orosius. Hier und u. 5 wohl ‘Kathedrale oder Abtei’ (vgl. Composita im Wb heafodmynster, -cirice); vermutlich hatte Verf. die Fortsetzung des eben kopierten Cnut-Satzes im Sinne

Ælfred uses heafodstede for Orosius’ capitolium. Here and below 5 probably ‘cathedral or abbey’ (cf. the compounds in the Wb heafodmynster, -cirice); presumably the author had in mind the continuation of the sentence of Cnut he had just copied
Neben Prälaten auch weltliche Magnaten laut 4. 5
Secular magnates as well as prelates, according to 4. 5

Der Schutz besteht hier, laut 4. 5, in Gewährung von Asyl (s. d. Gl 8a. 14a. 15), obwohl das Wort mund oder grið an sich nicht immer diese Sonderbedeutung zu haben braucht; s. Wb und z. B. to godum (Heidengöttern) þe mundbyrd secest; Cynewulf Juliana 170

The protection here consists, according to 4. 5, in the granting of asylum (see that word in Gl 8a. 14a. 15), although the word mund or grið need not in itself always have this special meaning; see Wb and e.g. to godum (heathen gods) þe mundbyrd secest; Cynewulf Juliana 170
Wer Asyl suchend die Kirche erreicht, erhält es be circan are; Af 42, 2. Vgl. Gl Kirchenrang 1
One who reaches the church seeking asylum is granted it be circan are; Af 42, 2. Cf. Gl Kirchenrang 1
